exposure: multiple triage visits (>=3) for suspected preterm labor or preterm premature rupture of membranes
outcome: severe neonatal morbidity or mortality before 120 days (composite)
cohort: The study included 1764 mother/newborn dyads whose mothers had been discharged after triage visits for suspected preterm labor or preterm premature rupture of membranes between 20 0/7 and 34 6/7 weeks gestation.
finding: Multiple triage visits (>=3) for suspected preterm labor or preterm premature rupture of membranes were not associated with significant differences in primary composite severe neonatal morbidity or mortality, or secondary neonatal and maternal outcomes.
mod_finding: Delivery via cesarean section was assessed as a secondary maternal outcome and found to have no statistically significant difference between the groups with multiple vs. fewer triage visits.
birth_weight: Average birth weight was 3056 ± 639 g for the more frequent visit group and 3048 ± 678 g for the less frequent visit group.
gest_age: Patients included in the analysis were between 20 0/7 and 34 6/7 weeks gestation at the time of their triage visits.
